text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign Minister Ljubomir Frckoski said on return from New York that U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan agreed to take part in the Forum for Europisation of the Balkans to be held in Macedonia this spring. Annan supported Macedonia's candidacy as non-permanent Security Council member.

- Socialist party leader Ljubisa Ivanov overnight dismissed several members of the party leadership. There are deep rifts within the party over whether it should continue to participate in the government coalition.

- Ethnic Albanian Party of Democratic Prosperty to stay in the government coalition for the moment. "Our abandoning the government will lead to destabilisation of the country. We need serious dialogue with Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski over open issues such as use of Albanian language in parliament and wider participation of Albanians in the government administration, PDP president Abdurahman Aliti said.
- Number of workers employed in industry down by 23.5 percent in 1996 compared to 1995, according to official statistics.
